reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates interstitial carbon activating TWIP/TRIP in a metastable dual-phase HEA, but the hypothesis applies this to a completely different alloy system (disordered BCC refractory HEA) without any direct evidence that the mechanism transfers. Key premises about BCC-specific stacking fault energy modification, avoidance of carbide embrittlement at the specified concentration, and maintenance of yield strength are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Interstitial carbon can activate TWIP/TRIP mechanisms in high-entropy alloys
TWIP/TRIP mechanisms improve strength–plasticity balance without sacrificing yield strength
The effect observed in a metastable dual-phase HEA generalizes to a disordered BCC refractory HEA (NbZrTiHfMo)
Carbon-induced lattice distortions and stacking fault energy modification promote nano-twinning/TRIP in BCC matrix
A narrow carbon range (0.3–0.5 at.%) avoids carbide embrittlement while enabling the mechanism
